title.en: The Secret of the Machines (Rudyard Kipling)

text.en: Machines tell us what they can do and who they really serve.

The poem begins by telling how machines are made and how they should be treated. Then the machines speak and explain how they serve humanity: they can do great deeds and heavy work.
The poem ends with the idea that the machines, however powerful, are still only creations of the human brain. It is a comment on technology and automation.
Notice personification, because machines speak. Learn the words automation, deed and creation.
